_comment: Roles for local models served by Ollama: which installed model does which job, under a name people
can pick. Copy it, and set each base_model_id to a tag that `ollama list` shows on that machine;
installed tags are machine-specific, so keep the copy out of git.
The fields are the ones Open WebUI's workspace models take (id, base_model_id, name, description,
an optional system prompt), so a script can create one named model per entry. Raw tags listed in
hide_base_ids are hidden from the model picker, leaving only the named roles.
The models named here are examples of each role's size and kind, not requirements. See
COORDINATION.md, Local models, for what a small local model is and isn't good for.

models.name: Research assistant
models.description: For research chats. A build of the base model with the organisation's research constraints and tool-use instructions as its system prompt (an Ollama Modelfile), so no extra system prompt is applied here.

models.name: Fast chat (default)
models.description: The low-latency default: an instruct model of about 4 billion parameters that answers without a reasoning pass. For everyday chat, routing and tool calls.

models.name: Deep reasoning (slow)
models.description: The same size of model with its reasoning pass on: it reasons at length before every reply or tool call, so it is many times slower. For hard reasoning where latency doesn't matter; not for tool-heavy work.
